## In brief

- This ledger claims no application code, product capability or slice approval. Slice S0 has begun: the entries under "Task and gate evidence" record the repository scaffolding and its checks, and nothing else is built.
- The documentation pack was drafted, reviewed by models of other makers, and corrected on 2026-11-11. Every first review ended in REJECTED; the corrections are listed below with who made them.
- The privacy document was reviewed four times by three makers. Its last ten corrections were made by the lead and have not been reviewed by another maker (open item OI-37, a precondition of slice S5).
- One objection of two reviewers stands unresolved by design: layout signals are outside the acceptance model of the privacy audit (open item OI-36).
- The corrections made after the final read-through have not been confirmed by another maker (open item OI-38, for the slice S0 gate review).
- A typed-decision qualification was measured on 2026-11-11; its set and caveats are preserved.
- PENDING rows are not claims of completion. Entries are append-only from the first commit on; a correction is a new row naming the row it corrects.

## How the pack was made and checked

"Maker" means the company whose model did the work. A writer and the reviewer of its text were never the same maker. The lead (a Claude model, Anthropic) planned, briefed, ruled on every finding and verified every returned file; it did not review its own rulings.

## Evidence rules for later entries

1. Record the exact command, its real exit code, the full commit hash, the date and who ran it.
2. For tests, add passed, failed and skipped counts and every seed or relevant environment limit.
3. For a reviewer, record maker and model, the reviewed commit and the unchanged verdict.
4. Never turn PENDING into a date or a pass without evidence. Never estimate an exit code.
5. Record new or unresolved work in [OPEN_ITEMS.md](OPEN_ITEMS.md), not as progress.
6. Keep personal names, attendee details and quotations out of this public ledger.
7. An evidence entry names the tested work commit. It is added by a ledger commit on the same branch that changes only ledger files (PROGRESS.md, OPEN_ITEMS.md and the status lines of TASKS.md), so the pull-request head differs from the tested commit by ledger text alone, and the checks are run again on that head. The reviewer's verdict and the merge record of a task are entered by the next pull request. Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-11.
8. A continuous-integration run is cited by its full link, never by a bare run number.

    File: scripts/check_tree.py
    Line: 201-207
    Wrong: `git ls-files -s -z -- <source>` treats the tracked filename as a Git pathspec, and the code takes the mode from the first returned record without verifying its path. For a nested `.gitignore` beneath a directory containing pathspec metacharacters, such as `docs/a[b]/.gitignore`, the query can return `docs/ab/.gitignore` instead. A non-regular index entry for the named source can therefore be accepted as regular, breaking the staged-state contract and allowing the guard to pass falsely.
    Fix: Query with a literal pathspec, require exactly one NUL-delimited record whose path equals `source`, and parse that record’s mode and object ID; read the staged blob by that object ID so mode and content are bound to the same entry. Add a black-box test containing `docs/a[b]/.gitignore` and `docs/ab/.gitignore`, with the bracketed source staged as mode 120000 while its work-tree path is a regular same-byte file, and require a `tracked-ignored` failure. Prove the test fails before the fix, then run unittest discovery, `python3 scripts/check_tree.py` and `python3 scripts/check_docs.py`, all with exit 0.

Findings F5 and F6 are confirmed fixed. F7, a defect in the lines of the last fix, was applied as written by the same builder of another maker than the reviewer (Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high`, xAI): the index is queried with a literal pathspec, exactly one record whose path equals the source is required, and the mode and the object id are taken from that record. In the same round, by a further decision of the owner of 2026-11-12, the comparison of a tracked `.gitignore` with its staged content is made by object id and no longer by raw bytes: the id of that index record against the id git would stage for the work-tree file (`git hash-object`), so that a checkout with line-ending conversion compares equal; that one call runs with the checkout's own git configuration. The class of F7 was closed in the same round, by a further decision of the owner: every git call of the check that is given a path takes it literally: the index is queried with git's literal-pathspec option, `git check-ignore` (which refuses that option for every path) gets each path with a `./` prefix, and the blob of `.env.example` is read by the object id of its one literal index record, so its mode and its content come from one entry. Nine black-box tests were added. Seven were written before the change, and five of them failed on the old check: a pair of folder names for which the old check read the wrong record, a CRLF work-tree file with `core.autocrlf` set in the repository, the same with the setting in a user-level file, a tracked file named `:.env`, and tracked files whose names begin with pathspec magic; the other two, the reviewer's own pair and a control with CRLF and no conversion, pass on both. Two more were added after the builder's hand mutants showed two conditions without a failing test: a synced pair of bracketed names that must pass, and a test of the index-record function that refuses a record whose path is not the source. No existing test was changed.

This breaks portable, closed preflight behaviour.
    Fix: Convert a non-null shutil.which result to an absolute path relative to the lookup process before returning it. Add a process-runner test with a relative PATH entry and a distinct child cwd that proves the originally located executable runs, then run the Python guard suite and ./eii test.

    Line: 84-90
    Wrong: Percent-decoded user, password and database fields are accepted when they contain a NUL byte. After pg_isready accepts, Popen receives that value in the psql environment and raises an uncaught ValueError, so preflight prints no FAIL result and violates the plan's no-raise probe behaviour.
    Fix: Decode the three fields once and reject any containing a NUL byte with a fixed, non-secret parse reason before constructing DbTarget. Add cases for %00 in user, password and database proving probe_postgres returns fail without starting a child, then run the Python guard suite and ./eii test.
PROPOSED OPEN ITEMS:

    Wrong: The stub writes the echo payload and marker without a newline or flush, then sleeps. When the timeout path sends SIGKILL, the pipe-buffered output is discarded. The added `r08_timeout` and `r09_timeout` cases therefore pass without exercising retained partial stdout or stderr, so the earlier finding and the approved R10 planted-violation requirement remain unsatisfied.

Parts 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10 were approved. The lead judged the six findings of parts 1, 3, 6 and 9 valid. Part 1's three lines were corrected by the lead; parts 3, 6 and 9 by two Claude Opus editors on disjoint files, checked by a Claude Sonnet verifier (six of six fixed). A close-out applied the requests that the disjoint ownership left (docs/02, docs/10, docs/12, docs/07), checked by a Claude Sonnet and a Claude Opus verifier. While making the attacker-view model of the stayer index exact, the editors found that draws which PRV-42 and PRV-43 share between stayer bills of nested or overlapping units and of different pairs of months are not modelled. The owner's note of 2026-11-12 settles it under point 3 of the owner's scope decision (each period gets the same disclosure control; defences against differencing across periods go to document 17): for version 1 the stayer bills keep the ordinary leaf treatment with the draw of their own cell key; the index is released only at municipality level or coarser (by sector where counts allow) and only where its stayer count passes the threshold; the exact sharing of draws is a stated limit of the audit (document 06, section 17) and item DHA-25 of document 17. With the current partitions, which hold no municipality unit in the money and quartile tiers and no protected split by activity, version 1 releases the index at national level only.

Row D5 of decision record 0016, which this pull request creates, now reads pay by occupation (Synthetic) and national mean pay and wage trends by economic activity (Public, item 9): its earlier words named middle ranges by sector, which no source of version 1 holds, because the Public tables give national means (PUB-78) and the owner's answer of 2026-11-12 rules out a protected split by sector.

Parts 1, 2, 5, 7 and 9 were approved. The lead, Claude Fable 5.2, judged the six findings of parts 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 and made the fixes.

- Part 3 F5, part 8 F3 and part 10 F3 (the partition of each municipality pay statistic): valid. Documents 07 and 08 now say one partition, not one family, and the mean names both additive families of its money-partition rows (MTH-55, MTH-76; the fixture of TST-197 plants a mean with one family only); the labour-market texts of documents 09, 10 and 11 state the mapping.
- Part 4 F5 and F6 and part 6 F5 (decision record 0018 item 12 on keys). The lead found the cause in the decision record itself: item 12 said that no service is called through any key during the build, while the owner's note of 2026-11-12 that it records speaks of the API keys held in the uncommitted `.env` file and does not name the provider key of the typed-decision gateway. Item 12 now states the note's scope and leaves that key to decision 0014 and OI-18. Under it the gateway passages of documents 02 and 16 that part 4 cites do not contradict the decision and stay as they are; document 02 names decision 0018 in its status, as the finding asks, and one stale phrase about the main model key is corrected. Part 6 F5 is valid under either reading and is fixed: the OI-01 summary of document 06 states the current rule, and its status names decision 0018.
- For the same reason the round-3 fixes of part 1's findings F13 and F14, which had applied the words "any key" to the gateway, are restored to the texts reviewed before (the two configuration rows of document 13, OI-34, the goal of S1-T08 and its line of document 14). OI-18 now puts the question to the owner: whether the gateway's provider key may be used during the build. No keyed provider run is made before the owner answers.
- Proposed items. Part 1 P2: the glossary's egress record now says that a blocked request keeps only the hash of the proposed payload. Part 1 P3: document 13 no longer says the model cost is measured once the key exists; it is measured at go-live. Parts 1, 5, 6 and 9 (the full test run was on the parent of the reviewed head): from this round the lead runs `./eii test` on the head itself and gives the output in the evidence file of the review.
- Fix commit `14d64dc659a24f546c2032c8dfb277af94c2221c`; the checks of the status row above ran on it.

#### S0-T06: fix round 1

- Lead's ruling on F1 (valid): the module itself promises that no part of a value is printed. The path of a refused content stays visible in the ordinary case, so that the developer learns which file holds the value, and is withheld when it holds eight or more consecutive characters of a guarded value. The reviewer's own fix withheld every path.
- Lead's ruling on F2 (valid in part): the tests keep one picture of the real repository's hooks folder and configuration before and after, because the task must prove that no test changes them (decision H10 of the plan; the owner's local hooks are never touched); but the test code opens no file there. The picture now holds the names, sizes and modification times of the hook files, the size of the configuration file and the answer of git to one question about core.hooksPath. The modification time of the configuration file is left out on purpose: another git command, a push that sets an upstream for one, rewrites that file without changing it. The reviewer's own fix removed the picture of the real repository. The lead's review brief had said that the tests cannot reach that folder, which was looser than the plan's decision; the round-2 brief says what the picture reads.
- Build round 2 (the builder of round 1, Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high`, xAI): two tests first, each red on the reviewed code (the path was printed; the function snapshot did not exist); then the eight-character window in show_path, the picture by file status only with one planted violation in a scratch repository (a hook rewritten with the same length, then core.hooksPath set), its three callers, and one sentence of the README. 60 hook tests.
- Lead's change after the builder's return: the picture of the configuration file holds its size only (see the ruling on F2).

- Kind of change: documentation only (decision record 0019 and the amendments it makes to the pack); it belongs to no task of TASKS.md and adds the tasks that build what it decides
- Writer persona: senior technical editor of the pack, with a principal privacy engineer for the privacy rules and a senior quantitative methods engineer for the method cards
- Reviewer persona: principal reviewer of specifications, privacy rules and calculation methods
- Source of the decisions: the owner's decisions and answers of 2026-11-12 (project records held by the owner)

- Record written by: the lead (Anthropic, Claude Fable 5.2), who settled each place where the owner's words met an existing rule and wrote the rule texts of item 25
- Pack edits: Claude Opus editors (Anthropic) for 06_PRIVACY_AND_DISCLOSURE_CONTROL.md and 07_ECONOMIC_METHODS.md, Claude Sonnet editors (Anthropic) for the other groups, on disjoint files, in two passes: the record as first written, then the owner's evening answers (forecasts of the released monthly statistics with PRV-54 amended; the catchment split by category and distance band; the places source read from its public copy)
- Third pass by the lead, after reading the rule texts, the privacy document and the nine new method cards in full: a forecast of a released series is computed in the product plane at request time; a catchment split in which a single competitor is still left after the merges is not shown; the reason key `forecast_below_zero` joins the contracts; the caption of a forecast range counts each past value against the range that the other past errors give, because a range from the smallest to the largest error holds every past value by construction; night-time radiance for an area is the mean of card C36 in every document
- Reviewer maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `gpt-5.6-sol-high` (OpenAI), read-only, in parts (a maker that wrote none of it)
- Skills and rules: the lead used project-orientation, task-standards, github-flow and strict-reviewer; each editor received the record, the lead's sheet of fixed names and class rules, and the list of passages of its own files
- Branch: `docs/decision-0019`
- Pull request: https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/17

#### Decision record 0019: fix round 1

- The lead ruled on the findings in one sheet, so that every document says the same thing. A base rate is Observed (counts over a stated period, with its own caveat key); the site estimate is Inferred, of the least-real class of its inputs; the night-lights figure of an area is the mean of the frame-cell values, Public and Observed. People present by pay band keeps its formula, and the text no longer says that people with no wage record get no band: the band shares are those of the unit's covered earners, and the caveat says what the figure assumes. Every forecast is computed at request time by eii_core.calc from released rows, like a projection, with no forecast table; the metric keys of the new figures are in the data contracts. The catchment split states its two end cases wherever it states the merge rule. A public build without the night-lights key continues and leaves the layer out. The refusal of a forecast, estimate, share, score, rank or fit for a named real place, building, business, owner or person is one case of the decline class. Every other finding is fixed as its Fix line says, in the narrowest form.
- The owner's answer of 2026-11-12 on the places copy is applied in the same round and closes OI-96: the copy dated 2025-01-10 is used for version 1 as it is and is shown with its date; no account is opened and no newer release is fetched for now; where a place of the copy disagrees with OpenStreetMap or Overture, the newer source wins. Item 21 of the record and PUB-102 say how that acts: in the de-duplication the record of the newer source is kept; OpenStreetMap points are still not merged, and where the reviewer's cross-check against them disagrees with the copy, the reviewer follows OpenStreetMap. TST-239 and task S2-T15 carry the planted duplicate pair.
- Editors, each on its own files and from the rulings: Devin command-line tool, `glm-5-3-high` (Zhipu AI), the data contracts; Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI), the methods, the privacy document and the record; Devin, `kimi-k3-1-pro-medium` (Moonshot AI), the back end and the assistant; Cursor, `composer-2.5` (Cursor), testing, the reviewer checklist, the runbook, operations, the open items, the documents index and the glossary; Devin, `deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017-high` (DeepSeek), TASKS.md and the implementation plan; Antigravity, `gemini-4-carbon-high` (Google), the brief, the architecture, the public data pack, the front end and the design direction; and Devin, `swe-2-high` (Cognition), the 23 passages of the owner's answer on the places copy.
- The lead's own changes: four wordings that two editors had touched outside any finding were restored; the phrase "interval or range" in summaries became "interval, range or counts" in 27 places by the lead's script; one row of the front-end document gained the end case of the catchment split by reference.
- Lead's checks: the documentation check; the agent files unchanged; searches for the statements that the rulings replace (none left outside the history lines of the closed item OI-96).

#### S0-T07: fix round 2

- The lead read every place the verdict names before ruling: the workflow rules module in full, the three plant-harness tests, make_copy, run_all, finding_is_known and the plan's table of planted violations. All three findings are valid in the form ruled below; the part of F2 on test_blocked_evidence_judgement is the first reviewer's F2 and was already fixed.
- Ruling G1 (F1): for the real workflow files the rule required-steps compared each job with itself, because its reference was read from the files under test, and sandbox_unchanged compared the sandbox workflow with a copy read at import. The closed reference is now the pinned text of the three workflow files: one SHA-256 literal a file in the rules module, reported first by the rule required-steps and used by sandbox_unchanged. A change of a workflow file changes its pin in the same commit, where a reviewer sees it. The reviewer's own fix was a literal table of normalized jobs and steps; the digest pins every byte of the same files with three literals instead of a second copy of the workflows. One planted violation removes the line that runs `./eii test` from a folder that is its own reference. The pin pattern ends with its anchor and applies to every `uses:` value.
- Ruling G2 and G3 (F2 and F3): the case table is validated by code that the harness calls before it makes any folder (guard names exactly the closed list in order, unique case names, registered plants), with a planted duplicate; make_copy refuses a destination that resolves to the root or to a folder that contains the root, with a planted test whose root is a scratch repository (on unfixed code a call with the real root would write into the checkout); the totals test plants one failed case among blocked ones, as the plan's table says. The reviewer's own fix also refused every destination inside the root; that is not taken, because a temporary folder may lie in an ignored folder inside the checkout.
- Ruling G4 (proposed item P1, ruled into the round): the lead's review question had asked for a finding that the known-line rule would wrongly leave out, and the reviewer constructed one. The judge looked a finding's line up with a wider line definition than the scanner's, so a line holding a carriage return before the known text could shift the lookup. The lookup now splits on line feed only; one planted test.
- The reviewer's proposed item P2 (an unused parameter of a test helper) is entered as a proposed open item by the next ledger.
- Fix round 2 (a stronger builder of a maker other than both reviewers, REV-40: the Codex command-line tool, `gpt-6-astra`, OpenAI): tests first, then the changes. The builder reported G4 as not fixed after the lead's first ruling on it, one changed line: its planted test, a real scratch history without a mock, still failed, because the git call in text mode had already turned the carriage return into a line feed. The lead's remedy was wrong and the test written first showed it; the revised ruling reads the file's bytes through a byte-mode call, splits on the line-feed byte and decodes the one line strictly.
- The lead's checks before the commit: nine breaks of G1 to G3 on a scratch copy, each caught by its test except one, the call of the validator from the run. The lead added that test (a planted table handed to the run is refused before any case runs) and one sentence of the README on the pins, and repeated the break of G4 after the revised fix.

### S1-T04 — Tile range-request spike: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/28 )

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): the FastAPI process serves one local tile artefact with HTTP byte ranges and no separate tile server (FE-58; the server half of FE-56; the `tiles` value of the health page, OPS-30). The artefact is 2,048 bytes of visibly synthetic text, not a map extract; the real extract is fetched later by the asset pipeline and served by the same route
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard product code
- Plan: a short plan by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (through the Devin command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings L-54 and L-56 override it where they differ. No separate plan review (the owner's rule for Standard tasks)
- Builder maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `composer-2.5` (Cursor): one build and two short completion passes after the lead's check
- Reviewer maker and model: Codex command-line tool, `gpt-5.6-sol` (OpenAI), read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); a full review
- Branch: `task/S1-T04-tile-range`
- What was built: `product/src/eii_product/api/` with `tiles.py` (the closed name form, the resolver that refuses anything outside the configured folder, the three-valued status rule, the router) and `app.py` (the application factory; the folder is an argument, so the module reads no environment variable); the fixture `product/tests/fixtures/tiles/spike.tile`; ten tests in `product/tests/` that speak HTTP to a real server on the loopback interface. `import eii_product` stays free of FastAPI. The route `GET /tiles` is provisional until task S3-T08 serves the health page, and says so in the module
- The rulings (L-54): `fastapi` and `uvicorn` are installed through the root dependency group `dev` with exact pins and the product manifest does not change, because the clean-environment guard of S0-T02 installs the three packages offline from an empty cache (OI-60); the gap is the new item OI-116. The browser half of FE-56 is not built here; it is carried by the tasks that render a map (the new item OI-115). The reference notes are not changed by this task; what it measured is listed below for task S1-T08
- The ruling L-56 on the one disagreement the builder reported and stopped on: the plan expected a malformed or a multi-range header to give the whole file or 416. The pinned FastAPI with Starlette answers 400 to `bytes=abc` and to `bytes=9-2`, and 206 with two parts to `bytes=0-1,4-5`. Accepted: RFC 9110, section 14.2, says "A server that supports range requests MAY ignore or reject a Range header field that contains an invalid ranges-specifier", and section 14.1.1 says "An int-range is invalid if the last-pos value is present and less than the first-pos" (www.rfc-editor.org, read on 2026-11-13). A rejection with no file content, after which the server answers the next request, is a safe failure, which is the third acceptance criterion. The request for two ranges is a valid request and is asserted as one, with the content of both parts. The plan's expectation was written before any run; the criterion decides
- Red run before the code: `test_full_request_returns_the_pinned_fixture` against an application with no tile route: 404 where 200 was expected
- What the lead's check found, and what the builder then changed in two short passes: (1) the digest of the fixture was computed from the file itself, so the plan's pin had no teeth: size and digest are now literals, and the builder saw the test fail with one changed digit; (2) the status of the fixture folder is asserted as exactly `ok`; (3) the builder had pinned `uvicorn` 0.34.3, a release of June 2025, and written "pypi 2026-11-13" as its source; the registry's own record names 0.54.0 as the current release, and with the old one the tests printed a deprecation warning of Python 3.14 three times. The pin is now the current release, the lock was made again, and the summary line of the tests is clean; (4) the name rule and the regular-file check of the route had no test: two tests were added, and the builder saw each fail with its check removed
- The lead's own breaks of `tiles.py` (nine; the file restored and compared byte for byte): before the second pass five were caught; after it eight are caught, each by a named test. The ninth, the explicit media type removed, is equivalent on this machine: the library's guess for the unknown ending gives the same `Content-Type`
- Measured, for the pin confirmation of task S1-T08 (the reference notes hold no field for these): FastAPI 0.162.5 resolves on Python 3.14 with Starlette 1.10.0; a satisfiable single range gives 206 with `Content-Range` and the exact bytes, and an end beyond the file is clamped; a range that starts at the file's size gives 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */2048`; malformed and reversed ranges give 400; a request for two ranges gives 206 `multipart/byteranges`; uvicorn 0.54.0 runs in a thread that is not the main thread and stops through `should_exit`. Pages the builder read on 2026-11-13: the Starlette page on responses (file response), the FastAPI page on custom responses, and the source of `uvicorn/config.py` and `uvicorn/server.py` in the uvicorn repository (its documentation site answered with an error at that time)
- Shared documents, entered by the lead in the work commit because six tasks of the slice are built at once: one sentence in README.md; the new items OI-115 and OI-116 in OPEN_ITEMS.md; the builder's own files name OI-116
- Hardening listed, not built (the plan's section 8 and the builder's return): conditional requests (`If-Range`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified`) and `HEAD`; `Cache-Control` and a tile address versioned by the release hash; a content security policy header on the page that loads tiles; seat authorisation on the tile route; a tile allow-list read from the release manifest; a policy for multipart ranges beyond what was observed; ranges over a compressed transfer encoding; serving the built front end and the glyphs from the same application; a size cap and a timeout on the tile route; a server socket handed over already bound instead of a free port chosen and closed first (the lead's addition, for the tests)
- With this ledger, because it is the first of slice S1: the closing record of the slice S0 gate above, and two proposed items of the lead's own in OPEN_ITEMS.md: PO-S1-04 (no test compares the tables of the documents with the lists the code holds: the cause of the gate's rejected first round) and PO-S1-05 (the hardening lists of the slice's task logs go into the register of document 17 with the follow-up task)

- F1, fixed: the answer to the request for two ranges is parsed by the boundary of its `Content-Type`; the test requires exactly two parts and compares the list of pairs (the `Content-Range` of a part, its complete payload) with `bytes 0-1/2048` and the first two bytes, `bytes 4-5/2048` and bytes four and five. The builder saw the test fail with the two expected pairs swapped, and restored
- F2, fixed: the complete body of each rejected answer is asserted beside its status: empty for 416 (with `Content-Range: bytes */2048`), and the fixed texts of the pinned Starlette for the two 400 answers ("Range header: range must be requested" for `bytes=abc`, "Range header: start must be less than end" for `bytes=9-2`). A returned slice of the file would change the body and fail. The builder saw the test fail with a changed literal, and restored
- F3, fixed: one helper sets `should_exit`, joins the thread and asserts that it is not alive; the module fixture and the four tests that start a server of their own use it. A new test, `test_stop_uvicorn_server_rejects_threads_that_survive_join`, hands the helper a thread that waits on an event nobody sets and requires the assertion error. The builder had typed that call with a suppression comment; the lead replaced the comment by a two-line protocol type for the helper's first argument, so the file holds no suppression (the lead's one edit; lint, format, strict types and the eleven tests pass)
- F4, corrected here; the earlier entries stay as they were written (TST-171). Three statements of the first ledger of this task counted wrongly: the line "What was built" of the task log said that ten tests in `product/tests/` speak HTTP to a real server; the note of the entry of `./eii test --seed 2026111311` spoke of "the ten product tests of this task"; and the note of the entry of `uv run --locked python -m pytest product/tests -v -p no:cacheprovider` said "The other seven" and then named five. The right counts at the first work commit `f2a42479d6c1efce3bb030e72c309ba9ff6bde7a`: the product suite held ten tests, of which eight were this task's (seven in `product/tests/test_tiles_range.py`, all over HTTP against a real server, and one pure test of the status rule in `product/tests/test_tiles_status.py`) and two were the tests of the package skeleton from task S0-T02 (`product/tests/test_product_package.py`). Beside the three tests of the acceptance criteria the task therefore had five further tests, not seven. At the fix commit the task has nine tests (the helper's own test is the ninth and uses no HTTP) and the product suite eleven. The description and the squash message of the pull request carry the right counts
- F5, corrected here: the status of the task in TASKS.md said "done (pull request 28, merged 2026-11-13)" on a head that was not merged. It now says "in review (pull request 28)". From this task on, the status of a task says "in review" inside its own pull request, and the ledger of the next pull request sets it to done together with the closing record of the merge (the lead's rule for the rest of the run; the acceptance boxes are ticked in the task's own pull request, where the evidence for them is)
- Round 2 goes to the same reviewer, limited as REV-39 says: the five findings, defects in the lines changed since the reviewed commit, and the checks that are never limited

### S1-T07 — Offline typed-decision gateway: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/29 )

- What the task builds (slice S1): the provider-neutral contract of the offline typed-decision gateway of [decision 0014](docs/decisions/0014-typed-decision-gateway.md), behind the stage only: `gateway/` becomes the fourth workspace member, `eii_gateway`, used by tooling under `scripts/` and `evals/` and by nothing under `core/`, `custodian/` or `product/` (BE-102, DAT-126). Its answers are decision evidence only. No provider was called and no key was used during the build (OI-01, OI-18)
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard; it computes and shows no number
- Plan: a short plan by Cursor Composer 2.5 (through the Cursor command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings R1 to R6 of the build brief override it where they differ. No separate plan review (the owner's rule for Standard tasks)
- Builder maker and model: Codex command-line tool, `gpt-6-astra` (OpenAI): one build and one short completion pass after the lead's check
- Reviewer maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI), read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); a full review
- Branch: `task/S1-T07-gateway`
- What was built: in `gateway/src/eii_gateway/`: the closed vocabulary (five decision classes each with its one permitted effect, three kinds, six outcomes) and the request of tooling-owned inputs; the data policy; memo keys by hash and the two fixed, hash-derived option orders of a choice; the thresholds for ordering and flagging; the record schema with the exact field set of DAT-126, validated on write and on read; the record store that writes only under `evals/typed_decisions/runs/`; the setting `EII_DECISION_PROVIDER`, default `none`; three providers (`none`, which does no input or output and reads no key; a recorded provider that replays hand-written synthetic fixtures; a standard-library adapter of the configured provider); and the facade that applies the policy, the token cap, the memo, the two orders and the fallback, and writes one record for every admitted call. Beside it: a consumer guard (`scripts/gateway_import_guard.py`) with its planted consumers, 24 contract tests under `scripts/tests/gateway/` and three guard tests
- The rulings (the build brief): R1, the adapter of the configured provider uses the standard library only, is written and never called, and says in its module text that its request shape is unverified; no test, command or import path of the default suite reaches it. R2, the tests stay under `scripts/tests/` and `./eii test` gains no suite. R3, no section is added to the reference notes; the fixtures of the recorded provider are tiny, hand-written and visibly synthetic. R4, `gateway/` is the fourth member with no third-party dependency; the clean-environment guard, the metadata guard and the import-boundary tests keep their meaning and are extended to the fourth member where they hold the list of members. R5, rules 26 to 32 of AGENTS.md bind every line
- The four acceptance criteria and their tests. (1) Default `none` opens no network: `test_none_never_opens_socket` (socket construction and connection replaced by a failing stand-in while the package is imported and a request is decided; the outcome is `DISABLED` with the fallback, one record is written, and the adapter module is not imported) and `test_none_ignores_jev_key`. (2) Forbidden data classes are blocked: `test_visitor_typed_blocked` (seven declared classes outside the four cleared ones, each refused before a provider is constructed, with nothing written) and `test_cleared_classes_and_class_restrictions`. (3) Records use the closed schema: the six tests of `test_decision_record_schema.py` (the exact field set, unknown and missing fields, malformed values on write and on read, a folder other than the runs folder, a later human disposition). (4) Serving packages cannot import the gateway: the unchanged three-plane guard with its 34 tests, one gateway test beside them, and the new consumer guard with planted consumers in five folders and three import forms
- The lead's ruling on the first disagreement the builder reported and stopped on (recorded for the owner as OI-117): item 6 of decision 0014 says that every call writes a decision record, item 8 that the gateway refuses every input class but the four cleared ones, and the closed schema admits only those four in `input_class`. A refused request is therefore not a call: the gateway raises before a provider is constructed and before anything is stored, for a class outside the four and for a cleared class that the decision class does not accept. Nothing of a refused input is kept, not even its hash. No record holds the outcome `BLOCKED_BY_DATA_POLICY` in version 1; the alternative reading is written in the item
- Two further points the builder reported, both accepted: the pin row of the provider stays `recorded`, because the version check requires that state of an external row (the plan had suggested another word); and the adapter's request shape is unverified, since ruling R1 forbids any call. The files under `evals/typed_decisions/runs/` are ignored by git (the plan's rule), so the output of a run is committed only by a deliberate act; this is the second half of OI-117
- Existing guards that changed, and why none is weaker (REV-15): the clean-environment guard, the workspace-metadata guard with its field tables and the support of the Python checks now name four members instead of three; the forbidden dependency edges gain every edge between the gateway and the three planes in both directions; the planted "extra member" of the field tables, which had been called `gateway`, is now a member that does not exist. No assertion was removed
- Red runs before the code: `test_none_never_opens_socket` with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'eii_gateway'"; later `test_later_human_disposition_is_readable` with "automated records cannot supply human disposition" (the schema lets a person add a disposition later), then fixed
- The builder's break pass, as it reports: 392 generated breaks, 361 caught at once; tests were added for the 31 that survived; of 39 follow-up breaks 37 were caught and two were left unexercised because exercising them would import the adapter, which ruling R1 forbids; six more for the disposition rule, all caught
- What the lead's check found, and what the builder then changed in one short pass: (1) `scripts/tests/test_gateway_import_guard.py` could not be run on its own ("ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gateway_import_guard'": it relied on another test module to put `scripts/` on the import path); it now follows the convention of the other guard tests. (2) With the facade changed to accept a choice when only one of the two option orders was answered, every test still passed; `test_choice_missing_second_answer_applies_fallback_and_writes_record` now fails on that break (the builder saw 'DECIDED' where 'UNAVAILABLE' was expected, and restored)
- The lead's own breaks (eight run, each file restored): a forbidden class added to the cleared list; the policy check moved after the construction of the provider; `question_route` freed from team questions; the default provider changed to the adapter; a zero token cap no longer stopping the configured provider; records allowed outside the runs folder; the memo replay switched off; a choice accepted on one order. Seven were caught by a named contract test at once; the eighth is the point (2) above and is caught since the completion pass
- The lead entered, in the work commit: one sentence in the status paragraph of README.md and the corrected layout sentence (`gateway/` is no longer scaffolding); OI-117 in OPEN_ITEMS.md; two sentences of `gateway/README.md` that had pointed to the builder's report now name OI-117 and this file
- Not measured, said plainly: no provider answer, latency, accuracy or token use; the request shape of the adapter; the requalification of task S1-T08. The synthetic scores of the recorded fixtures are fixture values, not measurements
- Hardening listed, not built (the plan and the builder's return): confirming the endpoint, the wire schema, the route identity and the meaning of the token cap before any authorised live use; memo arbitration between processes and an index of the runs folder; a redirect policy, retry and rate limits and an operational audit for the adapter; the full human-labelled qualification and its drift intervals (S1-T08 and later); the sign-off check of the release build for activity mappings; a wider static resolution of consumers outside the three planes

### S1-T06 — Sandbox enforcement spike: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/31 )

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): the production boundary of the generator sandbox holds on the build machine, with no fallback (ARC-09, SYN-01, TST-61; rule 12 of AGENTS.md). The launcher and its profile tables of task S0-T11 are unchanged; this task adds the proof
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard, moved up in care because sandbox enforcement is a security control with no fallback: beside the builder's break pass the lead planted four violations in the real launcher and saw the new command fail on each
- Plan: a short plan by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol (written on 2026-11-12 through the Cursor command-line tool, before the owner limited that tool to other models), read by the lead; the lead's rulings R1 to R5 of the build brief override it where they differ. No separate plan review
- Builder maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI): one build; no completion pass was needed
- Reviewer, as planned: Devin command-line tool, Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro, read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); the record of the verdict names the reviewer that gave it
- Branch: `task/S1-T06-sandbox-enforcement`
- What was built: the command `uv run --locked python scripts/sandbox_check.py check-enforcement`, which runs seven parts and prints one line for each, then `sandbox enforcement: OK` or `sandbox enforcement: FAILED`: the bubblewrap version; the probe outside the sandbox (the sentinel file is readable there and a local connection succeeds: the tooth of TST-61); for each of the profiles `build-world` and `build-release` the same probe inside the sandbox (the sentinel unreadable, a loopback connection and an abstract socket refused) and the judgement of the profile's mount list; the offline load of the engine extensions inside the sandbox. A part that fails prints `FAIL`, its name and what differs, and the command exits 1; a part that does not run is a failure. And `scripts/sandbox_policy.py`: it reduces the argument list that the launcher generates to roles and modes (file descriptors and host paths are not compared) and judges it against a closed sequence that is written in the module and not read from the profile tables, so a change of a table that moves, adds or drops a mount fails the judge
- The three acceptance criteria. (1) Sentinel read and network attempts fail: the lines `profile build-world sentinel: OK` and `profile build-release sentinel: OK` of the command below, with the outside probe as their tooth. (2) Mount list matches policy: the lines `profile build-world mounts: OK` and `profile build-release mounts: OK`; the nine tests of `scripts/tests/test_sandbox_policy.py` with their planted mismatches. (3) Any enforcement failure blocks the task: the command exits 1 when any part fails (`test_check_enforcement_prints_success_and_blocks_each_part` and `test_check_enforcement_reports_policy_and_blocks_failure`), and the lead's four planted violations in the real launcher, below
- The rulings (the build brief): R1, OI-61 and OI-62 are confirmed as far as the proof passes and nothing is redesigned. R2, the pin record and the technology-stack rows of document 02 are not changed here; the version that passed is listed below for task S1-T08; document 05 is this task's own and records the mount list that was confirmed. R3 and R4, the texts for the shared documents and the hardening points go to the lead. R5, there is exactly one launcher; the policy module starts no process, and no check may pass by not running
- The lead's planted violations in the real launcher, each followed by the command (the files restored afterwards; evidence in the review pack): a read-only path bind of `/etc` added to the argument list: exit 1, "unrecognised: extra path-read-only mount, expected absent" for both profiles; the network namespace no longer unshared: exit 1, the sentinel part of both profiles fails because the loopback connection succeeds; the vault mounted read-only: exit 1, "vault: mode read-only, expected writable"; the root not sealed: exit 1, "root sealing: missing, expected sealed". The lead's seven breaks of the report and of the policy (the exit status forced to 0; a failed part not counted; the extension load reported without running; the mount judgement's problems dropped; a role outside the policy not reported; the closed table changed; the order not judged) are each caught by a named test
- The builder's break pass, as it reports: every condition of the new code broken once and caught, with one planted option added for a branch that had no test (an option outside the table of argument counts)
- Existing tests that changed (REV-15): one expectation of `scripts/tests/test_sandbox_argv.py` now reads the usage line with the third command name; `scripts/tests/test_sandbox_output.py` gained one test. No assertion was removed or loosened
- Red run before the code: `test_check_enforcement_reports_policy_and_blocks_failure`: the command name was refused as a usage error with exit 2
- Measured, for the pin confirmation of task S1-T08: bubblewrap 0.11.1 on the build machine (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 6.6 under WSL2; AppArmor not enabled there); the engine-extension folder `data/engine_extensions/`, whose check passes and whose files load offline inside the sandbox. The installed manual page of that bubblewrap does not describe the two descriptor-bind options that the launcher uses; its `--help` output does. The reference-note field "path of the project-local extension directory" is supported by these runs. `uv run --locked python scripts/ci_sandbox.py facts` exits 1 on the build machine because a package of the hosted runner's AppArmor profiles is not installed there; that command belongs to the hosted runner and is not part of this proof
- Shared documents, entered by the lead in the work commit: rule 44 of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (the new command); README.md (one sentence of the status paragraph, the count and the list of the root commands, one line of the command block, one paragraph on the proof); one sentence added to each of OI-61 and OI-62 (what was confirmed and what stays open)
- Hardening listed, not built (the plan's section 8 and the builder's return): authenticating the bubblewrap executable beyond its path and version; protecting mounted inputs against a host process that changes them while the sandbox runs; bounds for the in-memory scratch and extension mounts once budgets are measured; refusing writable ancestor folders under temporary mounts; separation against root, the kernel and a compromised sandbox runtime
- With this ledger: the closing record of pull request 29 above, and the status of S1-T07 in TASKS.md set to done

### S1-T05 — First two-store parity query: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/30 )

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): one portable named query is answered by PostgreSQL 18 and by DuckDB 2.0 with identical normalised output, and a deliberate difference fails (BE-20 to BE-24 for the normalisation; TST-41 and TST-42 for the comparison and its stated rounding; TST-167: no fallback for store parity). It is a spike under `scripts/`, not the query registry or the store selector of the product
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard; store parity is a control with no fallback, and the lead ran the two-store proof itself
- Plan: a short plan in the owner's new form (83 lines) by OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (through the Codex command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings R1 to R5 of the build brief override it where they differ. No separate plan review
- Builder maker and model: Codex command-line tool, `gpt-6-astra` (OpenAI): one build; no completion pass was needed
- Reviewer, as planned: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI), read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); the record of the verdict names the reviewer that gave it
- Branch: `task/S1-T05-store-parity`
- What was built: `scripts/store_spike.py` (the one named query, the translation of its bound list parameter for each driver, strict parameter names and types, two independent adapters); `scripts/store_spike.sql` (one portable SELECT with a bound list, a grouped integer sum, a decimal control, explicit placing of NULL and a unique final sort key); `scripts/store_spike_normalise.py` (integers exact; non-integral numbers as decimals at six places, half to even, a binary float first through its shortest text; text in NFC; dates; a comparison of fixture identity, columns, row count, row order, value types and every field, whose message names positions only); `scripts/store_spike_fixture.py` (fourteen fixed synthetic rows with an independent expectation computed in Python; the database address from `EII_DATABASE_URL` only and on the loopback address only; a temporary PostgreSQL table with C-collated text inside a transaction that is rolled back; a temporary DuckDB file written, closed and opened again read-only with external access off and the configuration locked); `scripts/tests/test_store_spike.py` (31 offline tests: a real DuckDB, a mocked PostgreSQL) and `scripts/tests/live_store_spike.py` (the two-store command)
- The rulings (the build brief): R1, the spike stays under `scripts/`, and `psycopg[binary]` at its recorded pin joins the root dependency group `engine` (only the word `state` of its pin row changes). R2, the reference notes are not changed; what was measured is listed below for task S1-T08. R3, the live commands need the project's database service, which only the lead starts and stops: the builder wrote them and their tests and did not run them. R4, a test that needs PostgreSQL is never skipped and never answered by one store: the offline tests prove binding, normalisation, comparison and every refusal, and only the live command proves the two engines
- The three acceptance criteria. (1) Both adapters answer: the lead's live run with the service up, below: both engines match the independent expectation and each other for the full list, the empty list, a list of one unit and a list whose one element carries quotation marks. (2) Rounding is explicit: `store_spike_normalise.py` states it in code (six places, `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, integers never rounded) and the offline tests `test_half_even_positive_negative_even_odd`, `test_decimal_comparison_is_after_rounding`, `test_float_uses_repr_before_rounding` and `test_large_decimal_does_not_use_ambient_precision` prove it. (3) A deliberate divergence fails parity: the lead's live run with `--diverge`, exit code 3 after a passing baseline; offline, `test_deliberate_integer_divergence_fails` and `test_complete_result_plants`
- The lead's live runs at the work commit, with this project's Compose service on the loopback port of decision record 0020, started and stopped by the lead with `./eii db-up` and `./eii db-down`, every docker call scoped to this project, other projects' containers not touched. The password is read from the lead's secret file into the environment of the run only; the output was searched for it before anything was kept. In order: the variable unset, exit 1 ("database environment missing"); the service down, exit 1 ("engine operation failed", no pass line); the service up, exit 0; the same command twice more with byte-identical output; `--diverge`, exit 3 ("field mismatch row=4 column=3" after the passing baseline); a wrong argument, exit 2; a count of tables named `spike_control` outside temporary schemas: 0; the service down again, exit 1. The engines that answered: PostgreSQL server version number 180006, DuckDB 2.0.0, driver psycopg 3.3.8. The role was the service's superuser, which exists from the first start; the application role is built in slice S3
- The lead's own breaks (twelve; each file restored): the comparison made blind to row order; rounding half up; no NFC; an integer and an equal decimal taken as the same; no row-count check; an unknown query name accepted; a parameter of another type accepted; an address off the loopback interface accepted; the DuckDB reader opened for writing; the live command returning success on a mismatch; the live command printing a driver's error text; NULL sorted first in the query. All twelve are caught by named offline tests
- The builder's break pass, as it reports: 150 breaks; three survived at first (the configuration lock of the reader, one of the two C collations, fixture values changed without changing their order) and each now fails a test that was added
- Red run before the code: `test_deliberate_integer_divergence_fails` could not import the comparison module. One test design was corrected by the builder and said so: a first float value did not tell `Decimal(float)` from `Decimal(repr(float))`; the value 0.0000025 does
- Measured, for the pin confirmation of task S1-T08: DuckDB 2.0.0 and PostgreSQL 18.6 return the same order for text sorted by byte value (C collation on the PostgreSQL side), including a composed and a decomposed accented label, an Arabic label, ties and NULL placed last; named parameters with a bound list work on both drivers (`%(name)s` with `ANY` for psycopg, `$name` for DuckDB), the empty list included; the registry's current release of psycopg on 2026-11-13 is 3.3.9, one patch above the recorded pin, which this task does not change. The reference-note fields "text ordering by byte value, by the parity query" and "first parity query on both stores" are supported by these runs
- In the builder's tool sandbox the full test command could not pass (a nested cache that is read-only there makes one command test fail, and the commit-hook tests cannot stage); the lead ran every command at the work commit, below. This is the tool's sandbox, not a random failure of the repository: the same commands pass on the build machine and in CI
- Shared documents, entered by the lead in the work commit: rule 44 of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (the live command and its form with `--diverge`); README.md (one sentence of the status paragraph, the count and the list of the root commands, two lines of the command block, one paragraph on the spike); one sentence added to OI-111 (the driver is installed; preflight still uses the client programs)
- Hardening listed, not built (the builder's return): the production roles, the release loading, a full query registry with a portability lint and full-table digests (slices S3 and later); connection pooling, concurrency and soak tests, a database in CI; a connection policy that constrains inherited client-library configuration and credential-file defaults

### S1-T03 — Isochrone, drawn-shape and grid spike: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/33 )

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): walk and drive areas at different hours of the day, a free-drawn polygon and a radius are each kept as an exact shape and turned into whole frame cells, with routing inside the process and no server (ARC-88, BE-82, PRV-10, SYN-53). Everything is fixture-only: an invented road network of 81 nodes and 144 edges, a table of 24 hourly speed factors with two distinct values, a frame of cells at two resolutions. It is a spike under `product/src/eii_product/areas_spike/`, not the area builder of the product
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard; the spike shows no number to a user, and the choice it makes for SYN-53 goes into a decision record at the slice gate
- Plan: a plan by Zhipu AI GLM-5.3 (through the Devin command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings of the build brief and the rulings L-58 and L-59 override it where they differ. No separate plan review
- Builder maker and model: Codex command-line tool, `gpt-6-astra` (OpenAI): six rounds in all, told plainly below
- Reviewer, as planned: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI), read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); the record of the verdict names the reviewer that gave it
- Branch: `task/S1-T03-areas`
- How the build went, because it decides what the spike measured. Round 1 installed the pinned routing engine, found no call of its Python interface that builds a routing graph, and built the task on the written retreat (another library, with a convex hull as the area). The lead did not accept that: the official README of the engine's Python package says that the wheel ships the graph builder as a program, and the technology stack allows the retreat "only if needed". Round 2: a generator of the spike writes the synthetic road network as an extract in the format the builder reads (a few protocol-buffer messages in compressed blocks, written by hand, no new package); the shipped builder makes routing tiles from it in about a quarter of a second; the engine reads them in process and routes on them. Round 3 tried the two hour mechanisms that SYN-53 names. Rounds 4 and 5 put the engine behind the functions the tests call, replaced the tests that had described the retired mechanism, and removed the retreat with its dependencies. Round 6 moved the generator from the test tree into the package and turned two assert statements of the engine module into explicit refusals (the lead's two points of structure)
- The hour mechanism the spike chooses for SYN-53 (ruling L-58; OI-120 for the owner; the decision record is the lead's to write at the slice gate): per-edge scaling of edge times. One set of tiles is built for each distinct hourly speed factor, from the same extract with every way's speed multiplied by the factor; equal factors share one set; walking always uses the unscaled set. Predicted speeds inside the engine were tried first and are not used: the tool that adds them ran, and requests with a departure time were answered without a timezone database, but two hours with the same factor gave different outlines, and the cause is not confirmed
- What may change when the engine changes (ruling L-59): the five acceptance criteria and the properties a user could see do not change. Three assertions of round 1 described the retired mechanism and were replaced or removed, each named in the builder's report: the per-edge travel-time attribute (replaced by `test_cutoff_keeps_reached_place_inside_and_far_place_outside`: a named place that the road reaches within the cutoff is inside the area, one beyond it is outside); the refusal of a one-edge network, which was the degenerate case of the convex hull (replaced by `test_single_road_has_engine_polygon`); a doubled assertion of the empty network (kept once, as `test_empty_network_refused_before_builder`). The recorded output of the spike had been made in round 1 from the retreat and had never been committed; it was recorded once from the primary engine, in a step of its own
- The five acceptance criteria and their tests. (1) Routing has no server: `test_routing_opens_no_server` (the tile sets are prepared first; then socket creation, connection and process creation are replaced by failing stand-ins for every hour of the fixture table). (2) The drive area changes with the hour through a fixture speed table: `test_drive_isochrone_changes_with_the_hour` (different factors give different areas, equal factors equal areas, a changed table changes the result, the walk area does not change), `test_walk_always_uses_unscaled_tiles`, `test_equal_factors_reuse_tiles`. (3) Each shape is also kept exactly: `test_each_shape_is_kept_exactly`, `test_exact_ring_is_the_engine_polygon` (the routed area is the engine's own ring, with only the order of the two coordinates exchanged), `test_circle_away_from_equator`. (4) The snapped output contains only whole frame cells: `test_snapped_output_holds_only_whole_frame_cells`, `test_center_containment_keeps_entire_cell`, `test_radius_includes_boundary_and_uses_pin_cell_center`, `test_empty_snap_is_refused`. (5) Deterministic fixtures pass: `test_deterministic_fixtures_pass` (two fresh computations are equal and equal the recorded output), `test_pbf_reproduces_committed_fixture` (the generator reproduces the committed extract byte for byte, pinned by size and digest), `test_bundled_builder_and_actor_read_graph`
- The lead's own breaks (twelve; each file restored; run again on the final code): the factor applied to walking; the factor not applied to driving; the cutoff doubled; the two coordinates of the engine's ring not exchanged; an empty network not refused; the snap keeping cells outside the frame; an empty snap returned; the radius excluding the cell on its boundary; a failed tile build ignored; an unknown mode routed; a drawn ring left in its given orientation; a non-positive factor accepted. All twelve are caught by named tests
- Dependencies: `h3` 4.5.0 and `pyvalhalla` 3.9.1 at the pins of the pack, and `shapely` 2.2.0 (a new row of the pin record with the label ASSUMPTION; the registry's current release on 2026-11-13), all in the root dependency group `engine` (ruling L-54; the product manifest does not change). `shapely` is imported only by the spike's tests, for containment and validity assertions that do not come from the engine; `numpy` is installed because it needs it. `h3` ships no type information and has a minimal stub file for the calls used; the routing package ships type files without the marker a type checker looks for, so one setting of the type check makes it read them for that package; no error is suppressed and no setting is relaxed. ### S1-T01 — Arabic glyph and label-order spike: task log (pull request https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/pull/32 )

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): on the pinned MapLibre GL JS 6.17.0 and deck.gl 9.4.1, Arabic map labels are drawn as connected, correctly ordered words from self-hosted font files, and a data hexagon lies under the labels (FE-46, FE-57; DES-10, DES-24). The page under `web/spikes/glyphs/` is synthetic and says so: invented geometry over an invented box, five invented place names in Arabic and in English, no real place, no basemap of a real place, no tile download. It is not feature UI
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard; it is the first task that puts a browser test and a visual comparison into the project
- Plan: a plan by Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro (through the Devin command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings R1 to R9 of the build brief and the rulings of two completion passes override it where they differ. No separate plan review
- Builder maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI): one build and two completion passes after the lead's check
- Reviewer, as planned: Codex command-line tool, `gpt-5.6-sol` (OpenAI), read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); the record of the verdict names the reviewer that gave it
- Branch: `task/S1-T01-glyphs`
- What was built: the page (its style with font faces, the synthetic fixture, one interleaved overlay on WebGL2 with a polygon layer placed before the first label layer, the worker served locally); a loopback server with a same-origin content security policy; guards as pure functions with their own tests; nine browser tests with the pinned Playwright 1.65.0 and its headless shell; an evidence recorder (three screenshots, the request log, the asset manifest) and its checker; four licence texts of the fonts. The browser tests run inside `./eii test` through the web checks and build the page themselves into a temporary folder, so no stale build can be tested
- The three acceptance criteria. (1) Arabic labels render from local assets: the tests `Arabic labels render from local assets`, `English labels render from the same local fixture`, `a remote font attempt is blocked`, `four local licence texts are served` and `an omitted Arabic face fails font readiness`; the request log of the recorder holds same-origin paths only and one planted remote address, blocked. (2) Hexagons do not cover labels: the test `hexagons sit below the first label layer` (one overlay, interleaved, the layer's `beforeId` equal to the first label layer, no WebGPU) and the screenshot of that view. (3) Visual evidence is recorded: the three screenshots, the request log and the asset manifest under `web/spikes/glyphs/evidence/`, checked by the evidence command; the native review of the five names and the three images is the owner's and is recorded as pending, and nothing written by a model is recorded as an approval
- The lead's rulings that changed after the first build, each for a cost the build made visible. (a) The browser lives in the uncommitted folder `data/tools/playwright/` at the repository root, as the project's other fetched tools do, and only the headless shell is fetched: inside the installed package folder it took 701 MB in every checkout and was deleted by every `npm ci`; it now takes 288 MB and is fetched once. (b) TST-91: pixels are compared only in the hosted job, and the baselines come from the suite's own capture in that job, not from the recorder's separate screenshot call. (c) The suite and the recorder build the page themselves: the hosted job had no step that built it and would have stopped. (d) `./eii test` gives the web suite an allow-list environment without the variable `CI`, so a comparison inside it would never have run in the hosted job: the allow-list is not widened, and the hosted job compares in a step of its own (`npm run test:spike:glyphs`, where the runner's `CI=true` reaches the suite). (e) The browser installer installs system libraries only in the CI environment: on any other machine no command of this project changes anything outside the repository (the lead's own edit, then covered by the builder with a test)
- What the lead's look at the first screenshots found: in the Arabic page the English notice showed its full stop on the wrong side, because the sentence inherited the page's direction. It is now an isolated left-to-right element inside the paragraph, with an assertion that fails without it; the evidence was recorded again
- The baselines (TST-91, TST-92). The first hosted run of the pull request, on the work commit, made the three captures, uploaded them and stopped at the comparison step, which named the missing files: https://github.com/albarami/economic-investment-intelligence/actions/runs/43345530556 . The lead copied the three files of that run's artifact unchanged into `web/spikes/glyphs/tests/baselines/`, in a commit of their own (`d98de43d4856fd9b34b6ddcd29a87b7c359696bb`). Each is byte-identical to the evidence screenshot of the same view that the recorder wrote on the build machine (the digests are in that commit's message), so on this page the hosted runner and the build machine draw the same pixels
- Measured, for the pin confirmation of task S1-T08 (the reference notes are not changed by this task): with MapLibre GL JS 6.17.0 the five Arabic names are shaped and ordered from local font files through the style's font faces, without the right-to-left plugin and without glyph files in the older format; the library's own type notes still say that shaping across cluster boundaries needs that plugin, so this is a statement about these five names until the owner's reading, not about every Arabic string. One `MapLibreOverlay` of deck.gl 9.4.1 in interleaved mode on WebGL2 draws a layer before the first label layer; its first insertion happens before the style has loaded, and the layer group appears after the first idle. No code path enables WebGPU. The registry's current release of `maplibre-gl` on 2026-11-13 is 6.18.0, one minor above the pack's pin, which this task does not change. Pages the builder read on 2026-11-13: the Playwright pages on CI and on browsers, the release page of the upload action, the MapLibre style specification on font faces, the deck.gl page of its MapLibre module, the registry pages of the two Noto font packages
- Not built here: the half of FE-56 with the live traffic provider on, which belongs to the task that builds the provider's adapter (OI-115). A wider matrix of browsers, operating systems and pixel ratios is listed as hardening
- Shared documents, entered by the lead in the work commit: rule 44 of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (four commands that run from `web/`); README.md; one sentence added to each of OI-22, OI-43, OI-48, OI-88 and OI-89; the new assumptions OI-118 (the two font packages of the map labels; where the browser lives) and OI-119 (pixels are compared in the hosted job only). The builder had edited the two agent files and the README in its second pass, against the brief; the lead took those edits out and entered the texts by its recorded edits
- Hardening listed, not built (the builder's return): a wider matrix of browsers, operating systems, font rendering and device pixel ratios, with a visual comparison of Arabic shaping beyond the pinned browser

    Fix: make the shared ordinary-page helper fail after page settlement when any captured request is non-same-origin, including the CSP-blocked planted URL, while retaining route abortion. - The lead's judgement: the finding is valid. The first build brief ruled that every request of the page goes to its own origin and that the test fails on any other (ruling R9); the helper `open` of `web/spikes/glyphs/tests/glyphs.spec.ts` collected the requests and never judged them, so the rule was proved only by the one test that plants a remote font, not by the ordinary tests. Nothing was argued away
- F1, fixed by the builder (Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high`, xAI) in one round, in that one file. The planted test `the ordinary page helper rejects a remote font attempt` was written first: it opens the English page with the planted remote font through the helper and requires the helper to reject with a message that names the foreign host; before the change it failed, because the helper resolved. The helper now records every request of the page and, after the page has settled, gives the list to the existing pure function `judgeRequests` with the page's origin and throws its detail when any request is not same-origin; the route still aborts such a request. The builder's runs showed that the content security policy stops the planted font before the route sees it, so the helper listens to the page's request event as well: without that listener the planted test fails
- The lead's own two breaks on the fix, each restored: with the line that throws on a bad verdict removed, the planted test fails; with the listener of the request event removed, the planted test fails. The browser suite holds ten tests and all pass with the fixture as committed, so no ordinary view of the page asks another origin for anything
- The test `a remote font attempt is blocked` is unchanged. No page, server, guard, workflow, baseline image or document changed in the fix commit
- What the reviewer said about the images, recorded as it stands: its tool reads through a shell and could not display the three baselines; it compared their three digests with the message of the baselines commit, with `web/spikes/glyphs/evidence/run.json` and with the evidence images, and read the three tests that define the views (its check REV-24). The lead has looked at all three images. The native reading of the five names and of the images is the owner's and stays recorded as pending
- Round 2 goes to the same reviewer, limited as REV-39 says: the finding, defects in the lines changed since the reviewed commit, and the checks that are never limited

- What the task proves (slice S1, the technical spike): the pinned MapLibre GL JS 6.17.0 and deck.gl 9.4.1 draw 110,000 hexagons and 50,000 moving particles on one map, and the page records its own frame times so that the frame rate can be measured where the pack asks for it, in a browser that runs natively on the host (TST-132, FE-88). The page under `web/spikes/performance/` is development-only and synthetic: an invented extent with no place name, a fixed seed, no basemap of a real place. It is not feature UI
- Class of the work (the owner's note of 2026-11-12 on value and cost): standard
- Plan: a short plan by OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (through the Codex command-line tool), read by the lead; the lead's rulings of the build brief and of one completion pass override it where they differ. No separate plan review
- Builder maker and model: Cursor command-line tool, `grok-4.7-high` (xAI): one build and one completion pass after the lead's check
- Reviewer, as planned: Devin command-line tool, Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro, read-only (a maker that neither planned nor built); the record of the verdict names the reviewer that gave it
- Branch: `task/S1-T02-performance`
- A re-plan made with this pull request (the lead's ruling of 2026-11-13; OI-122 for the owner). TST-132 asks that the frame rate is measured in a browser that runs natively on the host of the build machine, because a browser inside WSL can fall back to software rendering. The build agents do not start a program of the host, so the third criterion of this task ("the trace records 60 frames per second on the build machine") and the fifth of S1-T11 need one action of the owner. Left where they were, they would keep both spikes unmerged, and the rest of the slice behind them, although everything else of them is built, tested and reviewed. The two criteria moved word for word to the new task S1-T12, which depends on S1-T02 and S1-T11; S1-T08 depends on S1-T12 as well, so no pin that the frame rate decides is confirmed before the traces exist (FE-89). The slice gate statement is unchanged. TASKS.md and the task list of document 14 changed in the work commit. Nothing about frames per second is claimed by this task
- What was built: the page (one interleaved overlay on WebGL2 with a hexagon layer and a particle layer over a synthetic map, a scripted orbit, a recorder of raw frame timestamps); the trace contract as pure functions (closed shape; percentiles by nearest rank and the share of frame intervals strictly under 16.7 ms computed from the raw timestamps, never taken from the page's own summary; the gate: the full counts, the wall canvas of 1920 by 1080 at a pixel-ratio cap of 1, the gate profile of thirty seconds, no lost visibility, resize or lost context, a hardware renderer, a native browser on the host with its capture record, at least 95% of frames under the budget); a loopback server that prints one address, checks the origin and the size of a post, validates it and writes the trace under a name it makes itself; the evidence command; a test that the production build holds nothing of the spike
- The two acceptance criteria of this task after the re-plan. (1) 110,000 hexagons render: the browser tests `the smoke orbit draws both layers and records a trace` (the layer reports 110,000 drawn instances and the canvas holds pixels of the hexagon class), `isolating hexagons leaves the hex canvas nonblank`, `omitting one hexagon lowers the drawn count` and `hiding the hexagon layer reports no hexagon instances`, and the Node test `the hexagon generator returns the gate count at one resolution`. (2) 50,000 particles render: the same smoke test for the particle layer, `isolating particles leaves the particle canvas nonblank`, `omitting one particle lowers the drawn count`, `hiding the particle layer reports no particle instances`, `a frozen clock leaves the first particle in place` and the Node test `particles move with time and repeat the same seed`. The browser tests run a short orbit at the full counts inside `./eii test`; they assert counts and the trace contract, never a frame rate
- The evidence command today: it fails with `missing-native-trace`, exit code 1, and writes nothing (recorded below). No placeholder trace and no capture record exist
- The lead's check of the build found four gaps, closed in one completion pass. The new Arabic notice of the page was not marked as pending native review (REV-24): it now sits in a small data file with its mark, the README lists it for the owner's reading, and a test fails without the mark. The ordinary browser tests did not fail on a request to another origin when it was blocked before any response, the same gap as finding F1 of the review of pull request 32: one helper now opens the page for every test, records every request of the page and fails with the foreign address after the page has finished, and a planted test goes through that helper. And two rules had no test that failed when they were broken (the lead's breaks): a user agent that names a headless browser must not count as native, and a post above the size limit must be refused; each has its test now
- The lead's own breaks (eight; each file restored): a software renderer accepted; a short orbit accepted; reduced counts accepted; a trace with lost visibility accepted; any origin accepted by the server; the layer-set name not checked before the file name is built: these six were caught at once.   F1 (REV-16)
    File: web/spikes/performance/layers.ts
    Place: `mountScene(...).renderer`, lines 213-217; `judgeRenderer` in `web/spikes/performance/trace.mjs`, lines 195-203
    Wrong: The gate does not establish hardware-accelerated WebGL2 as TST-132 and the Performance budgets section require. `context.RENDERER` can be masked, while `judgeRenderer` accepts every nonempty renderer except strings containing three substrings. In particular, a native Windows software renderer such as `Microsoft Basic Render Driver` passes, so a software measurement can qualify as the native gate.
    Fix: Record `UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL` through `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info`, returning `missing-renderer` when no unmasked value is available, and reject Windows software renderers including `Microsoft Basic Render Driver` as `software-renderer`. Add a planted gate case for that renderer and a focused test whose masked and unmasked context values differ, then prove them with `node --test spikes/performance/tests/trace.node-test.mjs` and `npm --prefix web run test:spike:performance`.
  F2 (REV-18)
    File: web/spikes/performance/server.mjs
    Place: `evidenceId` and `receiveTrace`, lines 43-46 and 160-162
    Wrong: The filename contains only 32 random bits and `fs.writeFileSync` uses its default truncating mode. A collision therefore overwrites an existing trace instead of preserving the recorded native measurement, violating the server's trace-evidence data-handling requirement.
    Fix: Create the file exclusively with `{ flag: 'wx' }` and, on `EEXIST`, generate a fresh server-side name or reject without changing the existing file. Make the ID generator injectable for a planted collision test that asserts the original bytes remain unchanged and no existing path is reused; prove it with `node --test spikes/performance/tests/trace.node-test.mjs` and `npm --prefix web run test:spike:performance`.
